title: Rule Book does not explain the final winner or DRAW on tied total points
steps: Open RULE BOOK and read SHOWDOWN FORMAT, SCORING and TIEBREAK. There is no final-winner rule.
Finish ten seasons with Daniel at Arsenal and Nik at Liverpool. Daniel wins the Champions League in season 1; Nik wins it in season 2; neither receives any other Showdown points.
Give Daniel the better league position in the other seasons. The season wins are Daniel 9, Nik 1; total Showdown points are 5 each.
Open the final screen: it correctly displays DRAW. Return to the Rule Book and look for the rule explaining that outcome.
expected: The Rule Book says to add each manager's points across all seasons; the higher total wins the Showdown; an equal total is DRAW. It makes clear that season tiebreaks and season-win counts do not break a tied final total.
actual: The game correctly shows DRAW for 5–5 despite season wins of 9–1. The Rule Book describes only season tiebreaks and does not explain accumulated final points, the final winner, or a tied-total DRAW.
root_cause: The Rule Book stops after season scoring and season tiebreaks. The existing final-winner rule is not included.

fix.change: Add the final Showdown rule: Add each manager's points from every season. The higher total wins. If the totals are tied, the Showdown is a DRAW; season wins and season tiebreaks do not decide it.

script_output:
Season 10 of 10: final points Daniel 5, Nik 5; season wins {"Daniel":9,"Nik":1}.
Existing final rule: points are added across seasons; equal totals produce DRAW even with unequal season wins.
Actual final screen: DRAW. Rule Book: only season tiebreak rules; no final points rule or tied-total DRAW.
PROOF RESULT: Rule Book must state that the highest accumulated points win the Showdown and a tied total is DRAW.
Exit code: 1 (the missing final-winner rule is the expected failed check).
assumptions: This is a minor Rule Book omission; the final winner and DRAW code already handle the outcome correctly.
The proof uses normal Premier League clubs and valid manual season results.
The ten-season history is built by the real history and scoring rules; Chromium mounts the actual final screen from that completed game test history.
